original_question: For 2n >= 6, let K be a compact zero-measure subset of (0, infinity). Does there exist a C-infinity Hamiltonian H: R^{2n} -> R that is C^0-close and compactly supported isotopic to the quadratic irrational-ellipsoid Hamiltonian H_0 = sum lambda_j |z_j|^2 with positive rationally independent coefficients lambda_j, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for every energy value in K?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3.4 in Section 3.2 (“Conjectures and open problems”): the paper asks whether, for 2n ≥ 6 and a compact zero-measure set K ⊂ (0,∞), one can find a C^∞ Hamiltonian H : R^{2n} → R that is C^0-close and isotopic (with compact support) to the irrational-ellipsoid quadratic Hamiltonian H0, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for all energy values in K. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. It has the correct dimension restriction 2n ≥ 6; the correct type of prescribed set K (compact, zero measure, contained in (0,∞)); the correct model Hamiltonian H0 = Σ λj|zj|^2 with λj > 0 rationally independent, i.e. the irrational ellipsoid model used immediately before Conjecture 3.4; and the correct desired conclusion that a C^∞ Hamiltonian H, C^0-close and isotopic with compact support to H0, should have no closed Hamiltonian trajectories on every level with energy in K. This is exactly the one-step strengthening of Corollary 3.2 to arbitrary compact zero-measure K that the paper formulates as Conjecture 3.4. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))
missing_details: State the ambient symplectic model explicitly: the paper works in the standard symplectic vector space C^n ≅ R^{2n}, and H0 is introduced as the quadratic Hamiltonian whose unit level is an irrational ellipsoid. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

Spell out that “for energy values in K” means: for every a ∈ K, the level set {H = a} carries no periodic orbit (equivalently, no closed Hamiltonian trajectory). The paper defines an aperiodic value exactly by this level-set condition. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

Keep clear that compact support belongs to the isotopy, not to H itself. The paper says “isotopic (with a compact support) to H0”; it does not ask for H to be a compactly supported Hamiltonian. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

The surrounding discussion places this conjecture in the class of proper Hamiltonians on R^{2n}; if you want the question fully stand-alone, either mention properness explicitly or retain the perturbation-of-H0 framing, which is how the paper controls behavior at infinity. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

Do not strengthen the official statement to “K is exactly the set of aperiodic values.” That stronger wording appears only in the motivating paragraph immediately before Conjecture 3.4; the conjecture itself only requires absence of closed trajectories for all a ∈ K. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

If you want to mirror the nearby text literally, note that the motivating paragraph says the expected Hamiltonian should be smoothly isotopic to H0, while the displayed conjecture itself says isotopic (with compact support). ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))
refined_question: Let R^{2n} ≅ C^n carry its standard symplectic structure, with 2n ≥ 6, and let H0(z) = Σ_{j=1}^n λj|zj|^2, where λ1,...,λn > 0 are rationally independent, so that {H0 = 1} is an irrational ellipsoid. If K ⊂ (0,∞) is a compact set of measure zero, does there exist a C^∞ Hamiltonian H : R^{2n} → R, C^0-close and isotopic to H0 through an isotopy with compact support, such that for every a ∈ K the level set {H = a} carries no closed Hamiltonian trajectory? ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))
justification: The draft is not really aiming at the broader question posed at the end of Section 2 (“How large can AP_H be?”), but at the specific conjectural realization problem stated in Section 3.2 after the irrational-ellipsoid example. The paper first proves the one-level case in Corollary 3.2, derived from Theorem 3.1, and then says it is plausible to perform the same modification simultaneously on all energy values from a compact zero-measure set K ⊂ (0,∞), leading directly to Conjecture 3.4. So the nearest official target is Conjecture 3.4, not the broader page-4 meta-question. ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))
